A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of CUPID. Their methods, equations, experiments, figures, and appendices can be matched despite retitling and substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on Toys4K and GSO, conditioning ablations, and qualitative object, scene, and multi-view results, including appendix examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports pose-reconstruction fidelity measurements in Appendix A.1, Table 5.

M1.justification: The two-stage flow model, occupancy/UV representation, PnP pose recovery, pixel-aligned refinement, occlusion conditioning, and scene composition remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 documents the existing solver; it does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use ABO, HSSD, 3D-FUTURE, and Objaverse-XL for training and Toys4K/GSO for evaluation, with the same single-object, scene, occlusion, and multi-view coverage. The new pose-encoding diagnostic tests an existing component without establishing additional dataset or application coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the corresponding benchmark tables, ablations, and appendix comparisons. Table 4 renames the TRELLIS baseline to 'Baseline (w/o PAC)'. Expanded descriptions of OnePoseGen's components do not establish a different evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a decoded-UV pose-recovery evaluation using reprojection, relative rotation, relative translation, and field-of-view errors. Existing benchmark protocols and training settings are retained. Figure 5 newly discloses ground-truth intrinsics for LRM/LaRa rendering, without establishing that their evaluation settings changed.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds a focused diagnostic of how accurately camera poses survive UV-volume encoding and recovery. The conditioning ablation and its numerical results remain, but v2 Figure 6 removes the third qualitative example from v1 Figure 5. Diversity and scene analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new pose-fidelity analysis reports means and 95th-percentile errors, adding tail-distribution summaries beyond the existing mean/median reporting. These percentiles are not confidence intervals. Neither version reports benchmark run uncertainty, and the qualitative random-seed demonstration is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical numerical results. New Table 5 reports, for example, mean normalized reprojection error 0.0009 and mean RRE 0.46 degrees, alongside other pose errors and percentiles. Figure 1 adds a plush-toy reconstruction example, while one qualitative ablation example is removed.

T1.justification: The joint posterior, flow-matching objective, projection optimization, and feature equations retain the same mathematical content. The added DLT/SVD/RQ pseudocode documents the previously cited pose solver; no new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are presented.

C1.justification: Joint object–pose generation, pose-conditioned refinement, and the headline performance claims remain. V2 strengthens the applicability claim by explicitly promising multi-view and scene reconstruction without task-specific tuning or optimization in the abstract and contributions; these applications were already illustrated in v1.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly interprets monocular geometry alignment as a proxy for pose accuracy, attributes gains to both object modeling and camera prediction, and argues that intermediate point-map pipelines could be streamlined. It also explains canonical orientation as a learned mode of curated data. Existing mask, lighting, centering, and multi-view orientation limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds explicit DLT solver pseudocode and discloses ground-truth intrinsics for baseline rendering. Training hyperparameters and hardware information remain. However, it removes v1's reproducibility statement, including the CUDA implementation note, OpenCV calibrateCamera alternative, rendering-script guidance, and training/inference code-release commitment.

R1.justification: V2 adds Hunyuan3D 2.0 and removes the Gibson, Sekuler–Palmer, and OmniPart references. It expands criticism of fixed-camera representations and CAST's alignment pipeline while retaining the same broad research positioning and comparison families.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are substantially rewritten around joint object–pose modeling. Related Work moves from Section 5 to Section 2, explanatory passages are revised throughout, and Appendix A.1 gains internal headings. The ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements are removed.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column presentation, extensively resizing and relocating text, figures, and tables. V2 adds a first-page illustration, Algorithm 1, and Table 5, transposes Table 3, and reduces the qualitative ablation display. Most other visual results are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Table 5 and Algorithm 1 make the pose representation and recovery process easier to assess and reproduce, while the proxy-metric and ground-truth-intrinsic disclosures clarify evaluation. These are limited gains: main benchmark evidence is unchanged, the new diagnostic lacks a clearly specified evaluation population, and some reproducibility disclosures are removed. Overall, the added component validation and methodological clarity provide a modest net improvement.
